# Load packages

```{r load-packages, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(openintro)
library(lubridate)
library(glue)
library(dplyr)
```

# Exercises

## Exercise 1 — Create three vectors

**Goal:** Create vectors of different types and report their `typeof()` and `class()`.

```{r create-vectors, eval = TRUE}
character <- c("sushi", "pizza", "taco", "burger", "pasta")
numeric <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
mixed <- c(6, 7, 8, "coffee", "tea")
```

> The first vector is the type `r typeof(character)` and class `r class(character)` , the second vector is the type `r typeof(numeric)` and class `r class(numeric)` , and the last vector is the type `r typeof(mixed)` and class `r class(mixed)`.

## Exercise 2 — Bind the vectors into a data frame

**Goal:** Combine equal-length vectors into a data frame with `bind_cols()`.

```{r bind-cols, eval = TRUE}
character <- c("sushi", "pizza", "taco", "burger", "pasta")
numeric <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
mixed <- c(6, 7, 8, "coffee", "tea")
data_frame <- bind_cols("numeric" = numeric, "character" = character, "mixed" = mixed)
data_frame
```

> The type of the dataframe is `r typeof(data_frame)` and the class is `r class(data_frame)`.

## Exercise 3 — Unequal-length vectors

**Goal:** See what happens when `bind_cols()` receives vectors of different lengths.

```{r unequal-bind, eval = FALSE}
character <- c("sushi", "pizza", "taco", "burger", "pasta")
numeric <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
mixed <- c(6, 7, 8, "coffee")
data_frame_2 <- bind_cols("numeric" = numeric, "character" = character, "mixed" = mixed)
data_frame_2
```

> It fails since there is a different number of variables for each of the collumns, so one of the entries has nothing to bind to.

## Exercise 4 — Store unequal vectors in a list

**Goal:** Use `list()` to hold vectors of different lengths.

```{r make-list, eval = FALSE}
character <- c("sushi", "pizza", "taco", "burger", "pasta")
numeric <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
mixed <- c(6, 7, 8, "coffee")
my_list <- list("numeric" = numeric, "character" = character, "mixed" = mixed)
my_list
```

> List combines all of the collumns into a sequence in order, instead of "matching" each entry in a collumn to another.

## Exercise 5 — Character month coerced to factor

**Goal:** Observe the axis order produced when ggplot coerces a character variable.

```{r earthquakes-factors, eval = FALSE}
earthquakes %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = month)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Month of the year", y = "Earthquake count")
```

> The month variable is being coerced into an arbitrary order which ends up being its alphabetical order instead of the chronological order of the months. It's wrong becuase the months are in alphabetical order.

## Exercise 6 — Reorder factors with forcats

**Goal:** Practice `forcats` functions that change factor level order.

```{r earthquakes-forcats-1, eval = FALSE}
earthquakes %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_infreq(month))) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Month of the year", y = "Earthquake count")
```

> This uses the function fct_infreq which orders the month according to their frequency of earthquake counts.

```{r earthquakes-forcats-2, eval = FALSE}
earthquakes %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_rev(month))) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Month of the year", y = "Earthquake count")
```

> This uses fct_rev which reverses the order of the months based on alphabetical order, so reveresed alphabetical.

```{r earthquakes-forcats-3, eval = FALSE}
earthquakes %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_inorder(month))) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Month of the year", y = "Earthquake count")
```

> This uses fct_inorder which orders the month based on their entry order in the original dataset.

```{r earthquakes-forcats-4, eval = FALSE}
earthquakes %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = month %>% fct_infreq() %>% fct_rev())) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Month of the year", y = "Earthquake count")
```

> This uses fct_infreq and fct_rev to order the months by frequency, then reverse that order.

```{r earthquakes-forcats-5, eval = FALSE}
earthquakes %>% 
  mutate(month = fct_recode(month,
                            "1" = "January",
                            "2" = "February",
                            "3" = "March",
                            "4" = "April",
                            "5" = "May",
                            "6" = "June",
                            "7" = "July",
                            "8" = "August",
                            "9" = "September",
                            "10" = "October",
                            "11" = "November",
                            "12" = "December")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(as.numeric(month)))) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Month of the year", y = "Earthquake count")
```

> This uses fct_recode to manually change the order of months from January to December, then converts the months to numbers 1-12 with as.numeric.

## Exercise 7 — Build a character date with glue

**Goal:** Create a character date column and inspect its type.

```{r earthquake-dates, eval = FALSE}
earthquakes_new <- earthquakes %>% 
  mutate(date = glue("{year} {month} {day}")) %>% 
  relocate(date)
print(earthquakes_new)
typeof(date)
class(date)
```

> The 2nd line of code in this chunk is combining the year, month, and day into a single collumn called date using the glue function. The thrid line is relocating the new date collumn to the first position. The type is `r typeof(date)` and the class is `class(date)`.

## Exercise 8 — Plot character dates

**Goal:** See the problem of plotting a character date on a continuous axis.

```{r plot-1933, eval = FALSE}
earthquakes_new %>%
  filter(year == 1933) %>%
  ggplot(data = earthquakes_new, mapping = aes(x = date, y = richter)) + geom_point()
```

> The plot is messed up because the x-axis has the date labels all overlapping, making it unreadable.

## Exercise 9 — Convert the date string with lubridate

**Goal:** Use a `lubridate` function to turn the character date into a Date.

```{r earthquakes-dates2, eval = FALSE}
earthquakes %>% 
  mutate(date = ymd(glue("{year} {month} {day}"))) %>% 
  relocate(date) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = richter)) +
  geom_point()
  typeof(date)
```
